title: Add residency policy schema + validation (pinned_region/allowed_regions) and migrate existing org config
author: Benji Okafor
release_notes: Introduce residency policy schema (pinned_region / allowed_regions), validation, and org-config migration to unblock gateway enforcement and routing constraints.
description:
Summary: Implements the control-plane schema for hosted/dedicated data residency policies and validates them at write-time and load-time. Adds a one-time migration that maps legacy org region configuration into the new residency policy shape. This is the foundational change for upcoming gateway enforcement and smart-routing constraints.

Context / motivation: Enterprise customers are asking for deterministic regional guarantees. We’re standardizing on a single policy object stored in org config so downstream enforcement points (gateway, router, storage writers) can make consistent allow/deny decisions. This PR focuses on: (1) schema + validation, (2) precedence rules, (3) migration from legacy settings, and (4) unit tests.

Policy model (per ADR-042): - residency_policy.pinned_region: string | null - residency_policy.allowed_regions: string[] | null Precedence: pinned_region (if set) implies allowed_regions = [pinned_region] for enforcement purposes. If pinned_region is null and allowed_regions is set, enforcement uses allowed_regions. If both are null, no residency restriction is applied (current default behavior for non-enterprise orgs until rollout flips defaults).

Validation rules: - Region identifiers must be from the supported region enum (e.g., us-east, us-west, eu-west, eu-central). - pinned_region must be a single supported region. - allowed_regions must be a non-empty set of supported regions with no duplicates. - If pinned_region is set and allowed_regions is also set, allowed_regions must either be null or exactly [pinned_region] (to avoid ambiguous configs). - Disallow "global"/"auto" values at this layer; those should be expressed via null policy + routing defaults, not by special-casing strings.

Migration: We currently have legacy org fields used by hosted routing (org.default_region + org.region_allowlist in a few places). This PR adds a migration that: - If org.region_allowlist exists and is non-empty, sets residency_policy.allowed_regions = region_allowlist. - Else if org.default_region exists, sets residency_policy.pinned_region = default_region (conservative choice: previously most customers assumed a default region behaved like a pin; enforcement can later loosen via exception/allowlist if needed). - Leaves policy unset for orgs with neither field.

Operational behavior / compatibility: - Migration is idempotent and safe to rerun. - Migration emits a structured log with org_id and resulting policy shape (no customer data). - Read-path tolerates both legacy fields and new policy during rollout; write-path prefers new policy and will not reintroduce legacy fields.

Illustrative config example: Before: org.default_region = "eu-west" After: residency_policy = { pinned_region: "eu-west", allowed_regions: null }

Implementation details: - Adds ResidencyPolicy model to control-plane config schema. - Adds validator in OrgConfigService.UpdateOrgSettings and in config deserialization guard (fail closed on invalid persisted values to prevent silently accepting bad policy; returns 400 with field-level errors on update). - Adds migration script + integration hook to run on startup for the control-plane job runner.

Test coverage: - Unit tests for validator: supported region list, duplicates, pinned+allowed mismatch, empty allowlist, null policy. - Migration tests: mapping from legacy default_region and allowlist; idempotency; no-op cases.

Files / areas changed (high-level): - control-plane/config/schema/residency_policy.ts - control-plane/config/validation/residency_policy_validator.ts - control-plane/migrations/2025_01_28_residency_policy_from_legacy.ts - control-plane/services/org_config_service.ts - control-plane/test/residency_policy_validator.test.ts - control-plane/test/residency_policy_migration.test.ts

Follow-ups (not included here): - Gateway enforcement middleware (ENG-2842). - Router constraint changes for pinned/allowlisted orgs (ENG-2843). - Error code taxonomy + docs links in payloads (handled in later PRs).

Review notes: Please pay attention to the conservative migration choice of default_region -> pinned_region. If we think this is too strict for some legacy orgs, we should discuss flipping it to allowed_regions=[default_region] (functionally equivalent today) but it impacts how we reason about future cross-region fallbacks.

PR checklist: - [x] Schema + validator implemented - [x] Migration is idempotent and covered by tests - [x] No customer data logged - [x] Backward compatibility on read path (legacy + new) - [x] CI green

Conversation (highlights): Jordan Lee: The pinned+allowed invariant is good, but can we make error messages actionable for Console? Benji Okafor: Added field-level errors ("residency_policy.allowed_regions must be null when pinned_region is set") and standardized error keys; Console can map these directly. Michael Nguyen: Migration mapping default_region -> pinned_region feels like it could surprise orgs that were using default only as a preference. Benji Okafor: Agree; however, security requested conservative behavior. Added a log metric counter for migrated-to-pinned to quantify exposure; we can adjust if pilots show breakage. Marcus Lin: Please confirm we fail closed when invalid persisted policy exists (e.g., manual DB edits). Benji Okafor: Yes; config load will reject invalid residency_policy and mark org config as unhealthy, preventing serving with an unknown enforcement state. Ethan Park: LGTM. Make sure the supported region enum stays in a single place so gateway/router reuse it. Benji Okafor: Refactored to control-plane/config/regions.ts and updated imports.

CI status: build (pass), unit-tests (pass), lint (pass), migration-dry-run (pass). Merged via squash.
